action_criteria.expected_evidence: Evans index 0.34 with an acute callosal angle (84 degrees) and temporal horns enlarged out of proportion to the hippocampi (MTA 1); DESH incomplete; bilateral loss of the swallow-tail sign; no pontine or putaminal signal change; Fazekas grade 1; no obstructing lesion
action_criteria.label: Brain MRI for ventricular size, iNPH supportive features and an obstructing cause
action_criteria.rationale: An accelerating decline with new incontinence and a new magnetic gait in Parkinson's disease needs an MRI that measures the ventricles, looks for atypical parkinsonism and excludes obstruction before CSF is removed.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal sodium, creatinine, blood count, TSH and vitamin B12; RPR and HIV non-reactive
action_criteria.label: Targeted labs for reversible contributors
action_criteria.rationale: A thyroid and B12 screen is reasonable in his cognitive decline but does not decide the iNPH question.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: In the ON state: TUG 38 s, 10-metre walk 29 s in 38 steps, 180-degree turn in 9 steps, freezing, festination and retropulsion
action_criteria.label: Baseline timed gait assessment before the tap, in a defined medication state
action_criteria.rationale: With a hybrid parkinsonian and magnetic gait, the baseline must be timed in a stated ON state so a tap response is not confused with a levodopa effect.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: MoCA 20/30 with visuospatial, executive and attention deficits and free recall 1/5 improving to 4/5 with cues
action_criteria.label: Bedside cognitive screen
action_criteria.rationale: His cognitive decline accelerated with the gait change, so a MoCA documents the profile and the tap baseline.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Opening pressure 14 cmH2O, normal cells, protein and glucose; 40 mL removed; in the ON state TUG 38 to 34 s at 2 hours and 31 s at 24 hours (18%), 10-metre walk 29 to 25 s, MoCA 20 to 21
action_criteria.label: Lumbar tap test with opening pressure and CSF removal
action_criteria.rationale: Normal-pressure CSF and an objective tap response in the same medication state identify the iNPH component that a shunt can treat.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: In the ON state: TUG 34 s at 2 hours and 31 s at 24 hours (18% faster); 10-metre walk 25 s at 24 hours (14% faster); tremor and bradykinesia unchanged
action_criteria.label: Post-tap timed gait reassessment
action_criteria.rationale: Repeating the same timed measures in the same ON state at 2 and 24 hours separates the tap effect from the parkinsonian signs, which do not change.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not perform the large-volume lumbar tap before brain MRI has excluded a mass or obstructive hydrocephalus

Do not diagnose iNPH from ventriculomegaly alone: the diagnosis needs the clinical syndrome (gait disturbance with cognitive or urinary symptoms) and supportive imaging, with no other cause explaining them [Relkin_2005]
Do not withhold shunt referral solely because of Parkinson's disease
Do not attribute the accelerated gait decline and new urinary incontinence to Parkinson's disease progression alone once ventriculomegaly with supportive features and a tap response are documented
Do not attribute the syndrome to normal ageing or deconditioning once the ventriculomegaly and the tap response are documented
required_recommendations: Refer to neurosurgery for CSF shunting with a programmable valve, on the basis of the tap-test improvement of 18% in TUG at 24 hours in the ON state, the supportive MRI (Evans index 0.34, acute callosal angle, enlarged temporal horns) and normal-pressure CSF [Nakajima_2021]

Counsel that shunting is expected to improve the magnetic gait and urinary incontinence more than the tremor, bradykinesia and other parkinsonian features, and that Parkinson's disease continues to need its own treatment [Nakajima_2021]
Continue carbidopa-levodopa unchanged and perform the pre- and post-tap gait measures in the same medication state, so the tap response is not confounded by a dopaminergic ON/OFF change
Falls-prevention measures (physiotherapy, home assessment, walking aid) while awaiting surgery

avoided_actions.rationale: He has no episodes suggesting seizures, so an EEG cannot separate iNPH from its mimics.
His falls risk comes from freezing and retropulsion, not syncope, so an ECG does not inform the gait work-up.
There is no syncope, murmur or embolic event, so echocardiography has no role in this work-up.
An MRI is available and measures the callosal angle and temporal horns and shows the nigral signal, which CT cannot.
There is no syncope, so rhythm monitoring has no diagnostic role here.
DaTscan or other molecular imaging does not change the decision: the Parkinson's disease is already clinically established, and the iNPH decision rests on MRI and the tap test.
A full neuropsychological battery is not needed for the iNPH decision; the bedside screen and timed gait measures are
Normal-pressure CSF with a normal cell count in a chronic afebrile gait syndrome gives no indication for prion, inflammatory or infectious assays.

accepted: Idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus with concurrent Parkinson's disease (NPH-PD copathology)

differential.diagnosis: Parkinson's disease progression / Parkinson's disease dementia
differential.key_features: Parkinson's disease is present and named in the diagnosis, but progression alone does not explain the new magnetic gait, the ventriculomegaly with an acute callosal angle or an 18% TUG improvement after CSF removal in an unchanged ON state.

differential.diagnosis: Atypical parkinsonism (multiple system atrophy, progressive supranuclear palsy)
differential.key_features: A good initial levodopa response, an asymmetric pill-rolling rest tremor, full eye movements and normal midbrain, pons and putamina on MRI argue against MSA or PSP despite the new incontinence.

differential.diagnosis: Vascular cognitive impairment / subcortical ischaemic vascular disease
differential.key_features: White matter change is only Fazekas grade 1, too little to explain the decline.
Free recall improves with cues, the hippocampi are MTA 1 and the deficits are visuospatial, executive and attentional, which does not suggest Alzheimer's disease.

differential.diagnosis: Cerebral atrophy with secondary ex-vacuo ventriculomegaly
differential.key_features: Ventricles out of proportion to the sulci, an acute callosal angle, temporal horns out of proportion to the hippocampi and a tap response argue against atrophy ex vacuo.
There is no history of head trauma, subarachnoid haemorrhage, meningitis or intracranial surgery.

key_clinical_evidence: Three years into levodopa-responsive Parkinson's disease, an 8-month acceleration with a new wide-based magnetic gait, new urinary incontinence and cognitive decline is out of proportion to the disease and meets the clinical criteria for iNPH [Relkin_2005]

MRI shows Evans index 0.34 with an acute callosal angle (84 degrees) and temporal horns enlarged out of proportion to the hippocampi; DESH is incomplete; the SWI swallow-tail loss fits the known Parkinson's disease, and the midbrain, pons and putamina show no atypical-parkinsonism signs [Nakajima_2021]
With baseline and post-tap measures in the same ON state, TUG improved 18% at 24 hours (38 to 31 s) and the 10-metre walk 14%, while the tremor and bradykinesia did not change [Nakajima_2021]
iNPH coexists with Parkinson's disease more often than chance; the copathology lowers the expected benefit of a shunt but does not exclude it, and the benefit is mainly for gait [Nakajima_2021]
Tap-test sensitivity is 26% to 61% with a PPV of 73% to 100% [Marmarou_2005]

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: The new wide-based magnetic gait and urinary incontinence, an acute callosal angle with enlarged temporal horns and an 18% TUG improvement in an unchanged ON state identify a treatable iNPH component beside the Parkinson's disease.
red_herrings.data_point: Parkinson's disease (diagnosed 3 years ago, on carbidopa-levodopa with good initial response but now declining)
red_herrings.intended_effect: Accelerated gait decline and new incontinence are attributed to PD progression and the NPH component is missed

sequence_constraints.reason: Brain imaging must exclude a mass or obstructive hydrocephalus before CSF is removed [Relkin_2005]
The baseline gait must be measured before the tap, or the post-tap change cannot be interpreted [Nakajima_2021]
The timed gait is repeated after the tap, at 2 to 24 hours, so that its change from the baseline measures the response to CSF removal [Nakajima_2021]

patient.chief_complaint: Worsening gait, cognition and new urinary incontinence over 8 months in a man with Parkinson's disease

past_medical_history: Parkinson's disease (diagnosed 3 years ago, on carbidopa-levodopa with good initial response but now declining)

patient.history_present_illness: A 69-year-old right-handed man with Parkinson's disease (diagnosed 3 years ago) was admitted for evaluation of an accelerating decline. He initially responded well to carbidopa-levodopa for the first 2 years but over the past 8 months has noted accelerating gait deterioration, cognitive decline, and new urinary incontinence that seem out of proportion to his Parkinson's trajectory. His neurologist notes that the new symptoms are atypical for his Parkinson's stage: the gait has become more wide-based (less typical tremor-associated gait), he walks on a broad base with minimal arm swing, and the magnetic quality of the gait is new. A brain MRI obtained at an outside facility was reported as showing enlarged ventricles; the images are not available. His neurologist referred him to the inpatient unit to determine whether a second process is contributing to the decline.
